dependency_constraints.source: [readme:README.md] and PR example show `import numpy as np` / `np.random.binomial` usage.

numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When using the legacy interface `np.random.binomial` (and/or before the fix), for very small p the sampled values are all 0 (e.g., `x.max()` returns `np.int64(0)`).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: For the same inputs, the fixed `Generator.binomial` produces non-zero samples with mean approximately equal to `n*p` (e.g., `x.mean()` is `np.float64(2.25e-06)` vs expected mean `n*p` of `2.4999999999999998e-06`).
trigger_conditions: Legacy interface `np.random.binomial(n, p, size=sample_size)` with very small p: p=5e-17 and n=50000000000 and sample_size=20000000; observed samples are all 0 (pre-fix or when using the legacy interface).
Fixed `Generator.binomial` with the same very small p inputs yields non-zero results and mean close to `n*p` (post-fix).

oracle_clues: Bug fix description: “Fix handling of very small p in Generator.binomial. Use log1p to compute an expression of 1 - p with more precision.”
Unit test oracle: for the fixed method, `x.mean()` should align with the expected mean computed as `n*p` (given as `2.4999999999999998e-06`).
Legacy behavior oracle: “Before this fix, or when using the legacy interface, the values in x will all be 0: x.max() Out[30]: np.int64(0)”.
Correctness judging clue: the test compares sample statistics against the analytically expected mean `n*p` (shown in the example).

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Very small p regime in which p is extremely small (test uses p = 5e-17) and n is extremely large (test uses n = 50000000000, with sample_size = 20000000). Also described as “very small p” / “very small p in Generator.binomial.”
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: Tolerance is expressed as a 6-sigma threshold: the test requires abs(expected_mean - sample_mean) < 6 * sigma, where sigma = sqrt(n * p * (1 - p) / sample_size).
category_specific_evidence: Unit test for extremely small p in binomial: n = 50000000000, p = 5e-17, sample_size = 20000000; expected_mean = n * p; sigma = sqrt(n * p * (1 - p) / sample_size); test asserts abs(expected_mean - sample_mean) < 6 * sigma (after asserting expected_mean - 6*sigma > 0).
PR description/commit: “Fix handling of very small p in Generator.binomial.”

PR body includes observed failure for the legacy interface (before the fix): for the legacy interface, values in x will all be 0; example uses the same n = 50000000000, p = 5e-17, sample_size = 20000000; legacy: x.max() == 0.
PR body includes success for fixed Generator.binomial method: rng = np.random.default_rng(); x.mean() == 2.25e-06; expected mean n*p == 2.4999999999999998e-06 (same n and p as above).
Code change uses more precision for computing 1 - p: in distributions.c, binomial->r changes from exp(n * log(q)) with q = 1.0 - p to exp(n * log1p(-p)).
Legacy distributions uses an unaltered copy of random_binomial_inversion (legacy_random_binomial_inversion) in legacy distributions code to avoid changing the legacy interface.
reproduction_risks: Evidence does not specify dtype/precision behavior (e.g., float32 vs float64) or any numeric tolerance beyond the 6-sigma rule; reproductions may vary if dtype/precision differs or if different interfaces are used (legacy vs Generator/default_rng).
Observed failure (“all zeros”) is tied to the legacy interface; reproductions must select the same interface/algorithm path as described.
The tolerance is statistical (6*sigma) and depends on sample_size; using different sample_size changes sigma and therefore the acceptance criterion.
